We need a retrosynthesis route with at most 1 step (i.e., direct purchase of target? but target not buyable). So we need a single reaction from commercially available precursors to target. Must be within $125 total cost.

We need to find a reaction template that can produce the target in one step. The target is an ester: COC(=O)C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2. Looks like methyl ester of a cinnamyl-type acid with a trimethylsilyl phenyl group attached to a cyclobutene? Wait structure: COC(=O)C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2. Actually C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C) is a cyclopropene? No C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C) is a cyclobutene? Let's parse: C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C) is a cyclobutene? The SMILES: C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C) is a cyclobutene with a TMS attached to the double bond carbon? Might be a silyl-substituted cyclobutene.

But maybe easier: target could be formed via esterification of the corresponding acid with methanol. So we need the acid: OC(=O)C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2 (i.e., same but OH instead of OCH3). That acid may be commercially available? Search.
